## 2534c7164e36

**No issue found.** I generated 128 real Racket-labelled medium lessons, each with six demonstrations and one query (896 pairs total). An independent left-to-right three-panel overlay matched all 896 outputs. Of those pairs, 726 contained all eight possible three-panel occupancy states; 170 were other linked cases. Every lesson had at least one all-state demonstration.

I tested all five wrong panel-priority permutations. None survived all six demonstrations in any of the 128 lessons, so no alternative priority rule changed an unrefuted query. Generator SHA-256 is `eab765a3418f667520bfac6419a2730a4666dcb1e3fb54508c5cc117ef051ac5`; rule hash is `3d9402d2c7a5`. Evidence is in `checks/audit/2534c7164e36/audit_summary.json` and the retained `episodes.jsonl`.

Limit: this is a finite sample and the adversary set covered the five priority permutations, not every conceivable overlay program. The audit target was not changed.

## 2534c7164e36

**Issue found: held-out test leakage in ordinary generation.** `_PUBLIC_MASK_TRIPLES` contains all six published inputs and its own comment identifies them as five training triples plus one held-out triple. `_draw_linked_masks` samples that full tuple, then applies D4 symmetry. Reproduction: `generate(seed=0, sample_index=17, difficulty="medium")` yields linked panel masks `(17812, 55027, 65090)`, which are a D4 transform of `_PUBLIC_MASK_TRIPLES[-1]`, the held-out test geometry. A learner can therefore see a recolored/transformed copy of the query in synthetic training. Exclude the held-out triple from the linked sampling pool; generalized truth-table scenes already provide broad semantic coverage.

triage.reason: Both source-bound finding sections retained for future task owners. Local main-generator checks do not independently reproduce these audits. See REVIEW/intake-20261002-batch12.json.

## 2534c7164e36

**A2534-1 — Reproduced published-test geometry replay; evaluation-split question. No reproduced in-domain semantic or exact-control defect found in the checks below.** Findings only: no generator, rule, reference, or retained task file was modified.

The audited generator is version `3.0.1`, SHA-256 `eab765a3418f667520bfac6419a2730a4666dcb1e3fb54508c5cc117ef051ac5`, exactly matching the fresh audit assignment. Its canonical program SHA-256 is `3d9402d2c7a5a95e4e76a0cac9b607451694f4f32a7a501664be99032ab453e1`; the declared and executed rule hash is `3d9402d2c7a5`. The supported execution receipt separately records executed rule-text SHA-256 `d50159e18b52bb7e0a46b7540466ab118e08eee31799c0e63d694f973caacdc8`. All counts below refer to this unchanged source.

**Prior lead and reproduced observation.** The retained audit in `repo/generators/2534c7164e36/evidence/review_index.json`, from `review-080665b9e70e6cd0:v0001`, describes held-out geometry replay against these same generator bytes. I used that retained text as a lead; the original return ZIP was not opened and its SHA-256 was not available in the index. On this source, `generate(seed=0, sample_index=17, difficulty="medium")`, with no overrides, produces masks `(17812, 55027, 65090)`. An independent enumeration of the eight square symmetries matches exactly the unique published test geometry, with symmetry 5 (horizontal reflection followed by one clockwise quarter turn). The generator validator returns `[]`; the observed family is `linked`, and this input belongs to the documented generator domain. The replay uses divider/Q1/Q2/Q3 colors `4/8/6/2`. Its actual Racket output is:

```json
[[6,6,8,0],[8,6,6,8],[8,6,8,2],[6,2,8,6]]
```

This establishes replay of the geometry, but does **not** establish that a protected evaluation split has been contaminated. The selected ID has two canonical rows: a training-source row with five training pairs and one test pair, and an augmented-source row with six training pairs and no test pair. The replayed test input is also one of those augmented training inputs. Its inclusion in `_PUBLIC_MASK_TRIPLES` is documented. Excluding it is appropriate if downstream evaluation intends to hold out that original geometry; if all published pairs are deliberately available for training, replay alone is not an admission defect. That split policy remains a domain question, and the prior audit's unconditional leakage conclusion is not adopted here.

**Possible lookup shortcut and a concrete counterexample to it.** `probe.py` constructs a finite rival by recording the six unique published input/output pairs under their eight shared square symmetries, normalizing only the color roles. These 48 enumerations produce 48 distinct geometry triples. The rival returns the stored recolored output for a known triple and a zero grid otherwise; it does not apply the cellwise overlay law. It explicitly uses all six public labels, including the training-source test label. It fits all 6/6 unique canonical pairs and matches the replay above on 16/16 output cells. The generator has neither a `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` nor a `LESSON_COMPETITORS` declaration; no declared rival names were replaced by a copied list.

The rival was also checked against every usable pair occurrence in both selected canonical rows: 12/12 fit, representing the same six distinct inputs and consistent published outputs. The forced generalized draw `seed=0, sample_index=0, difficulty="medium", overrides={"scene_family":"generalized"}` is an in-domain counterexample to that rival. Its masks are `(58188, 33194, 4715)`, `self_check` returns `[]`, and the observer reports `generalized`. The rival returns a zero 4x4 grid, whereas Racket returns:

```json
[[2,7,9,9],[0,7,9,7],[9,9,0,0],[2,9,9,9]]
```

They disagree on 13/16 cells. Thus geometry lookup is a shortcut for the finite linked family, but this rival is not sufficient for the full documented distribution. The source advertises a 3:7 linked/generalized selection weight; this audit did not estimate the natural family rate or claim complete-lesson teaching coverage.

**Boundary probe, explicitly outside the declared generator domain.** A hand-constructed 4x14 scene with masks `(112, 76, 42)` uses equal nonzero dividers, three distinct nonempty monochrome panels, all four possible output colors, and both priority-overlap decisions. It contains seven of the eight occupancy states, omitting only simultaneous occupancy of all three panels. Racket executes it successfully and returns `[[0,1,9,9],[4,4,4,0],[0,0,0,0],[0,0,0,0]]`; the lookup rival returns zeros, differing on 6/16 cells. The validator rejects it only with `generalized scenes must witness all eight occupancy states`. This is a concrete restriction of generator support relative to the executable rule, consistent with the `AXES.scene_family` documentation and retained design note. It is not reported as an in-domain validator error. It would matter if arbitrary sparse overlays are an intended deployment domain.

**Checks and limits.** The exact `scene_family` override was exercised at seed `2534`, sample indices `[0,20)` separately for each of `easy`, `medium`, and `hard`, and each of `linked` and `generalized`: six strata of 20 draws, totaling 120 draws. In every stratum all 20/20 inputs passed the validator, all 20/20 observations matched the requested family, and there were 20 unique inputs within that stratum. No pooled uniqueness claim is made. Against the Python `rule_mirror`, the lookup rival disagreed on 0/20 linked draws and 20/20 generalized draws in each band. These 120-draw counts are Python probe results, not additional Racket executions. The supported Racket command evaluated exactly nine distinct inputs: two generated witnesses, one hand-constructed boundary, and six unique canonical inputs. All 9/9 executed without errors and matched the independent overlay calculation; all 6/6 canonical outputs matched their published labels. No full battery, task test suite, or lesson sampler was run for this findings-only audit.

**Evidence and exact commands.** `checks/audit/2534c7164e36/counterexamples.json` contains the three probe inputs, actual authoritative outputs, rival outputs, validator results, domain membership, generator/rule hashes, and generation arguments. `input.json` is the nine-grid reference batch; `racket.json` is the unmodified supported execution receipt. `probe.json` retains the canonical-source and sampling counts. The reproduction and comparison programs are `probe.py` and `verify.py`; `commands.json` contains three ready-to-merge `verification_commands`, all with exit code 0. Commands were invoked from the packet root; `run_with_racket.py` changes the actual reference working directory to `/workspace/scratch/d6c17eba5ae6/packet/repo`:

```text
python3 checks/audit/2534c7164e36/probe.py
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply 2534c7164e36 --input ../checks/audit/2534c7164e36/input.json --out ../checks/audit/2534c7164e36/racket.json
python3 checks/audit/2534c7164e36/verify.py
```

**Disposition:** reproduced geometry replay and an explicit support boundary, both requiring domain/split context before being called defects. **No issue found** in the sampled in-domain semantics and exact family controls; this is a bounded audit, not a proof of universal correctness.

triage.reason: Short brief and general feedback read under lightweight acceptance. Shared-tool requests considered for the portable-test/durable-receipt work. Prior failures and unscored solves retained; no training admission.
